name: Original Instrumental Soundtrack with Editable Strudel Source and WAV Master
promise: Compose one complete original soundtrack in the official Strudel runtime and deliver editable Strudel source, an official WAV export, a listening master, and evidence that the music works technically and for its intended listener.
summary: A music-first contract for turning a mood, reference, scene, product, game, or other listening context into an original instrumental soundtrack with a deliberate musical identity and arc. The agent studies reference qualities without copying them, composes a complete piece rather than a decorated loop, then clones the official Codeberg Strudel repository at the pack's reviewed revision and uses that local application to play and export the result. Metrics can expose silence, clipping, harshness, or a flat dynamic profile, but they never substitute for listening: the outcome passes only when a human reviewer has heard the actual master and accepts its musical fit. This pack stops at the soundtrack and its evidence; it does not create, edit, synchronize, mux, publish, or deploy the media it may accompany.
useWhen: A project needs an original instrumental soundtrack, ambient bed, theme, title cue, menu cue, or short musical piece that can be authored and revised as Strudel code.
The desired duration, listening context, emotional direction, and important references are known or can be clarified before composition.
A human is available to listen to the exported audio and decide whether the music actually fits.
Editable source, a reproducible official-runtime render, and a clean WAV master matter alongside the music itself.
notFor: Finding, licensing, downloading, or editing an existing commercial or royalty-free track.
Voiceover, dialogue, lyrics, singing, speech synthesis, podcast production, or audio restoration.
A video, animation, presentation, game, or website build; those are independent outcomes even when they later use this soundtrack.
Frame-by-frame scoring, beat synchronization, sound-effect design, muxing, publishing, or deployment unless a different outcome explicitly requests it.
Imitating a living artist, copying a protected melody, or treating a named reference as permission to reproduce its composition.
Replacing the locally cloned official Strudel application with strudel.cc, a custom partial renderer, simplified synthesizer, or hand-written approximation for the accepted export.

workstreams.name: Musical direction and emotional arc
workstreams.brief: Begin with the listener and the intended use, not with Strudel syntax. Clarify the duration, format, mood, energy, density, instruments or textures, material to avoid, and whether the piece must loop or resolve. Study approved references and community Strudel examples for transferable qualities such as restraint, harmony, space, motif, timbre, and form; never copy their melodies or mistake a title or genre label for a complete direction. Write a compact musical brief and sketch the whole emotional and dynamic arc before composing.

workstreams.name: Complete Strudel composition
workstreams.brief: Compose one complete piece whose form serves the approved brief. Establish a small amount of memorable musical material, let the listener learn it, then develop it through harmony, register, density, timbre, rhythm, or silence. Give every layer a musical job and leave room between voices. Build genuine contrast and progression rather than repeating one loop, stacking constant layers, or chasing every visual cut. Use the installed full-depth Strudel skills whenever the piece needs harmony, groove, effects, texture, automation, transitions, or genre-specific craft. Keep the source readable enough for another agent or musician to revise.

workstreams.name: Official render and listening review
workstreams.brief: Clone https://codeberg.org/uzu/strudel.git into a task-scoped local directory, check out the reviewed revision ebc25467c0f117a7e7b9b11378e21cac94d730fd, install its locked dependencies with pnpm install --frozen-lockfile, and launch that checkout locally. Load the complete source into the local official application, play it, inspect runtime errors, and export the audio through Strudel's own Export to WAV interface. Record the origin, commit, install command, launch command, and local application address. strudel.cc may be used only as a diagnostic fallback and cannot satisfy final-render evidence. Never substitute a custom renderer merely because it is faster. Preserve the untouched local official export, and disclose any mastering changes separately. Use measurements to find technical defects and suspicious sections, then give the real listening master to a human reviewer. Revise from what the listener actually hears; do not declare the music good because it parses or reaches a loudness target.

outputs: Musical brief with intended listener and use, duration, mood, reference qualities, emotional arc, constraints, and material to avoid
Editable Strudel source for the complete composition
Untouched WAV exported by the official Strudel application
Listening master plus a compact preview when useful
Runtime, duration, channel, sample-rate, clipping, loudness, dynamic-range, and provenance record
Human listening review with accepted qualities, requested repairs, final decision, and remaining limitations

expectations.statement: The soundtrack has a clear intended listener and use, duration, emotional direction, energy arc, reference qualities, constraints, and material to avoid before composition is judged.
failureModes: vibe word treated as a complete brief

expectations.statement: The exported soundtrack forms one deliberate musical whole appropriate to the brief, with an opening, development, meaningful contrast or progression, and an intentional loop or resolution rather than an accidental repeated sketch.
failureModes: ending feels cut off or arbitrary

expectations.statement: A listener can recognize a coherent motif, harmonic world, instrumental palette, and emotional identity, with each audible layer serving the piece rather than filling space.
failureModes: busy arrangement with no focal idea

expectations.statement: The complete source plays and exports without runtime errors through a local clone of the official Codeberg Strudel repository at reviewed revision ebc25467c0f117a7e7b9b11378e21cac94d730fd, with the untouched local official export preserved.
failureModes: official Strudel repository not cloned locally
strudel.cc used as the accepted export path
requiredEvidence: local clone origin and reviewed commit
locked dependency install and local launch record

expectations.statement: The delivered master has the intended duration, channels, sample rate, audible continuity, headroom, dynamic behavior, and clean start and ending, with no clipping, unintended silence, missing layer, or undisclosed processing.

A human reviewer has listened to the actual final master and explicitly accepts its musical quality and fit for the intended use; parsing, rendering, waveforms, and audio metrics alone cannot pass this expectation.

Another agent or musician can identify the final source, official export, listening master, preview, runtime provenance, processing, review decision, and limitations without reconstructing the session.
failureModes: multiple masters with no selected final

guardrails: Use references to identify transferable musical qualities; do not copy protected melodies, lyrics, recordings, or a living artist's distinctive style.

Clone https://codeberg.org/uzu/strudel.git locally, check out reviewed revision ebc25467c0f117a7e7b9b11378e21cac94d730fd, install its locked dependencies, and use that local official application for accepted playback and export. strudel.cc is diagnostic fallback only.
A custom renderer, partial Web Audio approximation, substitute synthesizer, or remote-only Strudel session cannot satisfy official-runtime evidence.

Record the clone origin, exact commit, locked install command, local launch command, and local application address used for the accepted export. Preserve the untouched official WAV beside any listening master.
Do not treat parsing, console logs, waveforms, loudness, spectral measurements, or dynamic range as proof that the music sounds good. The human reviewer is the ear.
Do not force the music to mirror cuts, transitions, or another artifact unless the brief explicitly asks for scoring or synchronization.
Use only samples and external audio with clear provenance and rights; disclose them in the handoff.
Do not silently mux the soundtrack into another artifact or publish, upload, deploy, purchase, license, or contact anyone without separate approval.
verification: Review the musical brief against the intended listener and use, duration, mood, references, emotional arc, constraints, and material to avoid.
Review the complete source and full-duration export for deliberate form, motif development, harmony, palette, contrast, progression, restraint, and ending behavior.

Verify the local clone origin and exact reviewed commit, install its locked dependencies, launch that checkout locally, then play and export the complete source through its official application while inspecting runtime errors and preserving the untouched WAV.
Probe the official export and listening master for duration, codec, sample rate, channels, clipping, loudness, dynamic range, unintended silence, and suspicious section-level differences.
Compare the official export with the listening master and disclose every post-processing change.
Have a human listen to the actual final master; record accepted qualities, failures, and requested repairs, then repeat the official render and listening review after material source changes.

Record ready, repair-required, or no-go. A missing local official checkout, revision mismatch, remote or custom final render, runtime failure, missing official export, unresolved required listening concern, or absent human review prevents a passing result.
